newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU extends list of opt-outs to flight noise rules.
newsitem.headline: EU extends list of opt-outs to flight noise rules.

text.p: European Union transport ministers agreed on Tuesday to extend an existing list of older, noisier aircraft from poorer countries allowed to use EU airports until April 1, 2002, diplomats and officials said.
The deal, which must go back to the European Parliament before adoption, names specific aircraft from 16 countries which may serve EU airports until the phase-out date.

Ministers also agreed to allow Berlin's Tegel and Tempelhof airports, which are particularly close to the city centre, to bar so-called chapter II aircraft immediately after the rules come into force.
Tuesday's decision adds to a 1992 list of exempted aircraft details of aircraft from 16 countries which failed to seek exemptions in time for inclusion in the 1992 legislation.

The countries affected by Tuesday's decision are: Algeria, the Dominican Republic, Egypt, Iraq, Lebanon, Liberia, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Swaziland, Tunisia, Uganda, Zaire and Zimbabwe.
